Factor Count Comparison: Model Fit, Parallel Analysis, and MAP

Source: R/factor_count.R
factor_count.Rd

Fits the exploratory common-factor model with one factor, two, and so on, and sets beside each count what bears on it: the fit of that model and the test of the previous count against it, its information criteria, the reduced eigenvalue at that rank against its parallel analysis reference, and Velicer's average squared partial correlation after that many components. The table applies no cutoff and chooses nothing: the lines beneath it state what each criterion shows, and the count is a judgment that combines them with theory and the interpretability of the rotated solutions, which fa_exploratory gives at a chosen count.

Usage

factor_count(
  data = NULL,
  S = NULL,
  N = NULL,
  items = NULL,
  max_factors = NULL,
  estimator = "ML",
  missing = "fiml",
  ordered = NULL,
  criterion = "BIC",
  conf_level = 0.9,
  B = 1000L,
  percentile = 0.95,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'dmar_factor_count'
print(x, digits = getOption("dmar.digits", 3L), ...)

Arguments

data

Numeric raw observations. Supply exactly one of data or S.

S

Named positive definite covariance matrix, with N.

N

Sample size for covariance input, or a reference sample size for the parallel analysis of incomplete raw data (see parallel_analysis).

items

The items to analyze, by name: columns of data, or rows and columns of S, which is then reduced to them, in the order given; only the reduced matrix need be finite and positive definite. NULL, the default, analyzes every column of data or of S. Names that cannot be read as at least three distinct items are refused with an error of class dmar_items_invalid (see dmar_metadata).

max_factors

The largest count fitted. The default is the largest count whose model keeps at least one degree of freedom, the largest \(k\) with \((p - k)^2 - (p + k) \ge 2\) for \(p\) items; a larger count is accepted up to the one with zero degrees of freedom, whose model reproduces the covariances exactly.

estimator, missing, ordered

As for fa_exploratory, which fits each count with rotation = "none", since the fit of a count does not depend on the rotation. The missing data method is resolved once, as fa_exploratory() resolves it, and the same method serves every fit, the correlations of the eigenvalues and the MAP, and the parallel analysis. With ordered items and no item value missing, leaving missing out fits the items as they stand (listwise deletion with nothing to delete), exactly as missing = "listwise" does, and the method attribute records "listwise"; with a value missing, ordered items require an explicit "pairwise" or "listwise", and leaving missing out is refused before any correlation, fit, or reference data set is computed.

criterion

The information criterion by which the proper counts are compared, as compare_sem compares a set of models: "BIC" (the default), "SABIC", "HBIC", or "AIC", in either case. IBIC and SPBIC, the information matrix based criteria of Bollen, Ray, Zavisca, and Harden (2012), are not offered: lavaan's exploratory fits carry singular information matrices (their parameterization counts the rotational constraints), which sem_information_criteria refuses for them.

conf_level

Confidence level of the RMSEA intervals, default 0.90, the conventional level, whose limits decide the tests of close and not close fit at .05 (see sem_fit_measures); conf_level = 0.95 gives 95 percent intervals. It sets nothing else: the Monte Carlo limits of the parallel analysis reference in the parallel_analysis attribute keep the 95 percent default of parallel_analysis.

B

Number of reference datasets for the parallel analysis, a single whole number, default 1000; 0 omits the reference, and the table then carries the reduced eigenvalues alone. A positive B must be at least the number parallel_analysis requires at percentile: 200 at the default 95th percentile, 1000 at the 99th, 100 at the 90th or at the median (at least 10 reference datasets beyond the quantile and never fewer than 100). A smaller positive B is refused before any model is fit (class dmar_count_invalid); see dmar_bootstrap.

percentile

Reference percentile of the parallel analysis, default 0.95.

seed

Optional seed for the parallel analysis; default NULL uses the current random stream. A supplied seed restores the caller's stream.

x

For print(), a table returned by factor_count().

digits

For print(), the decimal places of the display (default getOption("dmar.digits", 3); see dmar_tbl).

...

For print(), passed to print.data.frame().

Value

A dmar_tbl data frame (class dmar_factor_count) with one row per count: term, factors, solution ("proper", "improper", "no maximum", or "not converged"), chi_square, df, p_value, rmsea, rmsea_ci_lower, rmsea_ci_upper, cfi, tli, srmr, aic, bic, sabic, hbic, criterion_delta, criterion_weight, criterion_log_evidence (the comparison by criterion), delta_chi_square, delta_df, p_delta, eigenvalue, reference_quantile, exceeds_reference, and map. Its tidy() keeps the count as estimate and adds a conf_level column, the level of the RMSEA intervals (see dmar_tidiers), which glance() also reports. Attributes retain fits (the lavaan object of each proper count, NULL otherwise), fit_measures (each count's table, as fa_exploratory() returns it), parallel_analysis (the parallel_analysis table, when B > 0), comparison (the compare_sem table of the proper counts, when two or more were compared), map (the average squared partial correlation for \(m = 0, 1, \dots, p - 2\)), reasons (why a count has no proper solution), method, and analysis_note.

Details

The fit of each count. Each count is fitted by fa_exploratory with the same estimator and missing data method, and its fit_measures supply the chi square statistic with its degrees of freedom and p-value, the RMSEA with its interval, the CFI, TLI, and SRMR, under the same version policy (see sem_fit_measures; after FIML the indices are the corrected ones of Zhang and Savalei, 2023). The model with one factor fewer is nested in the model with one more, and delta_chi_square, delta_df, and p_delta give lavaan::lavTestLRT()'s test of the previous count against this one (the Satorra-Bentler scaled difference under estimator = "MLR"). The AIC, BIC, and sample size adjusted BIC are those of sem_information_criteria; smaller is preferred, and only the differences between rows carry meaning. Under estimator = "ULS" the statistic has no reference distribution, so the p-values, the RMSEA, CFI, TLI, difference tests, and information criteria are NA and the SRMR remains (see fa_exploratory).

Differences, weights, and evidence. The values of a criterion mean nothing on their own; what carries the evidence is the difference between two counts. The proper counts are therefore compared by criterion as compare_sem compares a set of models fitted to the same data: criterion_delta is each count's gap from the lowest value, criterion_weight is \(\exp(-\Delta/2)\) normalized over the proper counts, and, for BIC and HBIC, which approximate \(-2\) times the log marginal likelihood (Bollen et al., 2012), criterion_log_evidence is \(\Delta/2\), the approximate log Bayes factor of the best count over this one, and the weights approximate posterior probabilities under equal prior odds (Burnham & Anderson, 2004); for AIC the weights are Akaike weights and for SABIC they carry no further interpretation, so the log evidence column is NA for both. The weights are conditional on the set of proper counts compared, and the line under the table gives the best count, its weight, and how far the nearest other count stands from it. Every count is fitted to the same cases under the same missing data method and mean structure, which compare_sem() checks. The comparison needs two proper likelihood fits, so under ULS, or with one proper count, these columns are NA.

A count whose model does not converge, or converges to an improper solution (lavaan's post-estimation check fails: a residual variance below zero, or a covariance matrix that is not positive definite), or whose likelihood has no maximum (a residual variance runs off below zero while the likelihood is flat or still rising, and the optimizer stopped somewhere along the way; see fa_exploratory), has no fit to report: its solution column says so, its fit columns are NA, and a line under the table names it. Such a count is informative in its own right, since the unrestricted model with that many factors drives an item's residual variance to or below zero on these data, but it is not a stopping rule: the counts beyond it are fitted and reported in the same way. fa_exploratory refuses an improper solution for the same reason.

Eigenvalues and their reference. The eigenvalue column holds the eigenvalues of the reduced correlation matrix, the item correlations with the communalities of a fixed one-factor maximum likelihood solution on the diagonal, as parallel_analysis forms them; the reference_quantile is that function's percentile of the same eigenvalue in B independent normal reference datasets, and exceeds_reference compares the two (Horn, 1965). The correlation matrix is the one parallel_analysis() uses: the full information maximum likelihood estimate of cov_fiml for incomplete continuous items, the polychoric correlations for ordered items, the sample correlations otherwise. The reference percentile is a null threshold, not a confidence interval for an eigenvalue or a confidence statement about the count. The parallel analysis is run when every item is ordered or none is, which is the interface parallel_analysis() supports.

The minimum average partial. Velicer's (1976) rule extracts principal components of the correlation matrix one at a time, partials the first \(m\) out of it, and averages the squared partial correlations that remain; no component is retained after the average reaches its minimum. The map column holds the average after as many components as the row has factors; the map attribute holds it for every \(m\) from 0 (the average squared correlation itself) to \(p - 2\), and the line under the table names the \(m\) at which it is smallest. The rule concerns components used as a first-stage description of the common variance; it is reported beside the fit of the factor models, not as a substitute for it.

Display. The printed table, and knit_print() and as_kable of it, show one row per count with its solution status, the chi square statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value, the RMSEA with its interval (whose level the line beneath the table names), the CFI, TLI, and SRMR, the chosen criterion with its delta and weight, the p-value of the difference test against the previous count, the eigenvalue and its reference, and the MAP; columns with nothing to show (the reference when B = 0, the likelihood quantities under ULS, the comparison with one proper count) are left out. The table itself keeps every column. Beneath the table: the counts with the lowest AIC, BIC, and SABIC among the proper solutions, the criterion comparison, how far the eigenvalues exceed their reference, where the MAP is smallest, and the counts without a proper solution.

References

Bollen, K. A., Ray, S., Zavisca, J., & Harden, J. J. (2012). A comparison of Bayes factor approximation methods including two new methods. Sociological Methods & Research, 41(2), 294–324. doi:10.1177/0049124112452393

Burnham, K. P., & Anderson, D. R. (2004). Multimodel inference: Understanding AIC and BIC in model selection. Sociological Methods & Research, 33(2), 261–304. doi:10.1177/0049124104268644

Horn, J. L. (1965). A rationale and test for the number of factors in factor analysis. Psychometrika, 30, 179–185. doi:10.1007/BF02289447

Velicer, W. F. (1976). Determining the number of components from the matrix of partial correlations. Psychometrika, 41(3), 321–327. doi:10.1007/BF02293557

Zhang, X., & Savalei, V. (2023). New computations for RMSEA and CFI following FIML and TS estimation with missing data. Psychological Methods, 28(2), 263–283. doi:10.1037/met0000445

See also

fa_exploratory for the solution at a chosen count, parallel_analysis for the eigenvalue reference with its Monte Carlo limits, compare_sem for the comparison the criterion columns reproduce, and sem_information_criteria.

Author

Examples

items <- c("t1_visual_perception", "t2_cubes", "t4_lozenges",
           "t6_paragraph_comprehension", "t7_sentence", "t9_word_meaning")
# B = 200 is the fewest reference data sets the 95th percentile of the
# parallel analysis is reported from; the default is B = 1000.
factor_count(holzinger_swineford, items = items, B = 200, seed = 113)
#> Factor counts 1 to 2 for 6 items, N = 301
#> Estimator: ML; missing data: FIML; unrotated solutions (the fit of a count does not depend on the rotation)
#> 
#>  factors solution chi_square df  p_value                rmsea   cfi   tli  srmr
#>        1   proper    103.230  9 < 0.0001 0.187 [0.155, 0.220] 0.856 0.760 0.114
#>        2   proper      2.109  4   0.7157 0.000 [0.000, 0.064] 1.000 1.011 0.008
#>      bic delta weight  p_delta eigenvalue reference   map
#>  11054.5  72.6  0.000       NA      2.444     1.032 0.110
#>  10981.9   0.0  1.000 < 0.0001      0.568     0.170 0.102
#> (each count's model: chi square test, RMSEA with 90% interval, CFI, TLI, SRMR, BIC with delta (its gap from the lowest) and weight (its relative weight among the proper solutions); p_delta: the test of the previous count against this one; eigenvalue: of the reduced correlation matrix, with its parallel analysis 95th percentile; map: Velicer's average squared partial correlation after this many components)
#> 
#> Information criteria over the proper solutions: lowest AIC at 2 factors, lowest BIC at 2 factors, lowest SABIC at 2 factors.
#> BIC comparison over the proper solutions (compare_sem()): lowest at 2 factors, weight 1.000; the nearest other count, 1 factor, is 72.6 higher (weight 0.000, log Bayes factor 36.3 for 2 factors over it).
#> Parallel analysis (normal reference, B = 200, 95th percentile, reference N = 301): the reduced eigenvalues exceed their reference through rank 2.
#> Velicer's MAP: the average squared partial correlation is smallest after 2 components (0.102; before any component is removed it is 0.164).
#> 
#> Confidence level: 90%
#> 
#> No cutoff is applied and no count is chosen: the count is a judgment that combines the fit of each model, the difference tests, the information criteria, the eigenvalues against their reference, and the MAP with theory and the interpretability of the rotated solutions, which fa_exploratory() gives at a chosen count. Each model's interval and p-values condition on its own count, and the criterion weights are conditional on the set of proper counts compared.
